\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{چور} (chor)}{چور (chor)}]{\ur{چور} (chor) — a thief}

\label{lesson:UR-C276-chor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a fruit seller, then the Urdu for a greengrocer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{چور}}
\textbf{\ur{چور}} — \emph{chor} — \textquotedblleft{}a thief\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{چور} \ur{کھڑکی} \ur{سے} \ur{آیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chor khiṛkī se āyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief came in through the window.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{چور}} (\emph{chor}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{cōrá}, \textquotedblleft{}thief\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4931). It names a man or a woman: the verb shows which, \textbf{\ur{چور} \ur{آیا}} or \textbf{\ur{چور} \ur{آئی}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chor}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chor}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chor khiṛkī se āyā.} — The thief came in through the window.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a fruit seller, then the Urdu for a greengrocer, then say \emph{chor} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{چور} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A thief\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{چوری} (chorī)}{چوری (chorī)}]{\ur{چوری} (chorī) — a theft}

\label{lesson:UR-C276-chori}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a greengrocer, then the Urdu for a thief.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{چوری}}
\textbf{\ur{چوری}} — \emph{chorī} — \textquotedblleft{}a theft\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کل} \ur{رات} \ur{گلی} \ur{میں} \ur{چوری} \ur{ہوئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kal rāt galī meṅ chorī huī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a theft in the lane last night.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{caurikā}, \textquotedblleft{}theft\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4937). It sits beside \textbf{\ur{چور}}: the \textbf{\ur{چور}} is the person, the \textbf{\ur{چوری}} is the deed, and \textbf{\ur{چوری} \ur{ہوئی}} says that one took place.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chorī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chorī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kal rāt galī meṅ chorī huī.} — There was a theft in the lane last night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a greengrocer, then the Urdu for a thief, then say \emph{chorī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{چوری} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A theft\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{چرانا} (churānā)}{چرانا (churānā)}]{\ur{چرانا} (churānā) — to steal}

\label{lesson:UR-C276-churana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a thief, then the Urdu for a theft.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{چرانا}}
\textbf{\ur{چرانا}} — \emph{churānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to steal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{چور} \ur{نے} \ur{میرا} \ur{بٹوا} \ur{چرایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chor ne merā baṭuā churāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief stole my wallet.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کتاب} \ur{چرائی}, \emph{us ne kitāb churāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{چرانا}} (\emph{churānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{cornā} under Sanskrit \emph{cōráyati}, \textquotedblleft{}steals\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4933). With \textbf{\ur{نے}} the verb follows the thing stolen: \textbf{\ur{بٹوا} \ur{چرایا}}, \textbf{\ur{کتاب} \ur{چرائی}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{churānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{churānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chor ne merā baṭuā churāyā.} — The thief stole my wallet.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a thief, then the Urdu for a theft, then say \emph{churānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گواہ} (gavāh)}{گواہ (gavāh)}]{\ur{گواہ} (gavāh) — a witness}

\label{lesson:UR-C276-gavah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a theft, then the Urdu for to steal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گواہ}}
\textbf{\ur{گواہ}} — \emph{gavāh} — \textquotedblleft{}a witness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سب} \ur{کچھ} \ur{گواہ} \ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sab kuchh gavāh par munhasir hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everything depends on the witness.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
is usually traced to Persian \emph{gavāh}, \textquotedblleft{}one who bears witness\textquotedblright{}. A \textbf{\ur{گواہ}} saw what happened and says so.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gavāh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sab kuchh gavāh par munhasir hai.} — Everything depends on the witness.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a theft, then the Urdu for to steal, then say \emph{gavāh} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{واردات} (vārdāt)}{واردات (vārdāt)}]{\ur{واردات} (vārdāt) — a crime (as an incident); a raid}

\label{lesson:UR-C276-vardat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to steal, then the Urdu for a witness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{واردات}}
\textbf{\ur{واردات}} — \emph{vārdāt} — \textquotedblleft{}a crime (as an incident); a raid\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{اس} \ur{گلی} \ur{میں} \ur{دوسری} \ur{واردات} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih is galī meṅ dūsrī vārdāt hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This is the second crime in this lane.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{واردات}} (\emph{vārdāt}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{wāridāt}, \textquotedblleft{}things that arrive, happenings\textquotedblright{}; in Urdu the word has narrowed, it seems, to an incident of crime: \textbf{\ur{چوری} \ur{کی} \ur{واردات}}, a theft as the police report it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vārdāt}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yih is galī meṅ dūsrī vārdāt hai.} — This is the second crime in this lane.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to steal, then the Urdu for a witness, then say \emph{vārdāt} again
\end{itemize}
